confirmed_repair2_semantics: Raw script, style, and xmp closing tags use source-coordinate-preserving ASCII-only case comparison; U+0130 before a valid close cannot shift it and non-ASCII name lookalikes cannot close raw state.
Bikeshed ATX closing sequences are removed after explicit-anchor projection, and an ATX source line is never emitted again as a Setext heading.
Empty paired targets, ordinary quoted prose, invalid single-quote shorthands, and hostless schemes produce no semantic reference candidate.
Text and href specification URLs are admitted only after URL parsing and CSSWG/W3C-TR classification; non-specification hrefs receive one exact REVIEWED_EXCLUDED_NON_SPECIFICATION_HREF disposition.

Definition scopes are comma-split, whitespace-normalized, case-normalized sets with parsed-attribute provenance; generic HTML label-for never becomes a definition-scope owner, while a dfn's own for remains meaningful.
Definition-target joins use a scope/name index and materialize only disposition-INCLUDED relations.
All operation-ledger contract fields are type-checked; duplicate IDs and duplicate source URL/SHA/byte intervals are rejected before joining.

A non-null ledger owner_candidate must equal the source-derived heading owner; null is preserved explicitly as REVIEWED_UNRESOLVED, and admitted operations preserve the full reviewed ledger evidence fields.
The analyzer uses indexed raw-name, open-tag, range, preceding-heading, operation-ledger, and carrier relations instead of the rejected full-source fold and repeated depth/list scans.
The oracle independently uses generated ASCII-only raw-name regexes, declarative ledger validation, its own reference-shape predicates, and separately derived normalized owner relations.

eliminated_paths: whole-source Unicode lowercase followed by coordinate reuse
findLastIndex matching-close search in the analyzer
per-heading range scans from row zero
per-scalar Buffer.byteLength slicing in the analyzer byte map
output_sensitive_paths: A reference that legitimately resolves to C carriers must materialize C carrier IDs; total carrier-join output can therefore be quadratic in an adversarial many-to-many corpus.
Projected text over nested or overlapping malformed semantic containers can revisit source ranges in proportion to the requested output relations.
Candidate raw strings and full SHA-256 preimages are materialized, so nested or extremely long candidates can make emitted output bytes exceed source bytes.

Denominator shards, compatibility publication, authenticated launcher/runtime/dependency closure, and crash-fault custody remain absent.
